reason: The submitted CIF is valid but the exact atomic realization is not sufficiently established. It parses and symmetry-expands as primitive Pm (No. 6), Z=1, with the stated 5.83122 x 3.40162 x 12.83139 A cell (beta=92.2142 degrees), 14 fully occupied ordered atoms, and exactly Ag2Cr3NbS8. Indexing is strong: the trace's 28 isolated-line refinement gives 0.0019 degrees RMS in 2theta and no important line-position failure. Periodic chemistry also passes: there are no overlaps, Ag/Nb/Cr have complete six-S shells, and bond-valence analysis supports Ag(I), Cr(III), Nb(V), and S(-II); the submitted heavy-element ordering is also the best fixed-coordinate permutation. However, atomic-intensity support is not converged. The comparable-score report supplies no score, while the trace's instantiated selected-CIF profile gives Rwp about 10.75%. A blind angle-dependent pseudo-Voigt audit on the same indexed cell gives a Pawley/profile bound of Rwp about 4.24% (RMSE 0.208) but only about 7.21% (RMSE 0.354) for the instantiated CIF, with several major-peak residuals far above the measured baseline noise (sigma about 0.106). Moreover, the trace's later direct coordinate refinement produced a chemically viable unsaved Pm realization with lower full-range RMSE (0.5156 versus 0.5264) and coordinate shifts as large as 0.046 fractional, contradicting the claim that the submitted coordinates uniquely converged. The multi-start runs all reused the same prototype/deconvolved target and therefore were not independent maps, and Pm was not quantitatively tested against further symmetry lowering. Another attempt is likely to add a materially improved coordinate/symmetry realization even though the cell, framework family, and primary element ordering are credible.
